name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, known as the Scotland of the East for its rolling hills, pine forests, and colonial-era architecture. Serves as the main base for exploring waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges of the region.
facts: Capital and largest city of Meghalaya
Headquarters of East Khasi Hills district
Known for educational institutions and vibrant markets

name: Khliehriat
description: Headquarters town of East Jaintia Hills district, administrative and commercial center for the Pnar community in the eastern Jaintia Hills. Gateway to caves, waterfalls, lakes and wildlife areas of the district.
facts: HQ of East Jaintia Hills district since 2012
Main base for exploring district attractions

name: Moopun Waterfalls
description: Scenic waterfall on the Umjhai River at Mutong village, dropping about 110 feet into a crystal-clear pool, featuring a unique natural stone bridge above and rare pitcher plants on the rocks. Popular picnic and swimming spot.
facts: About 25 km equidistant from Jowai and Khliehriat
Natural stone bridge and swimming pool
Legend links to Umhang Lake and Water Goddess

name: Umhang Lake
description: Largest natural lake in the Jaintia Hills, located at Bataw (Wataw) village, surrounded by forests and offering views toward the plains. Associated with local legend of creation by chieftain U Sajar Nangli; revered by villagers.
facts: Largest natural lake in Jaintia Hills
About 29 km from Khliehriat via Rymbai
Created according to legend by Sajar Nangli
Sacred to local community; overlooks Bangladesh plains

name: Krem Liat Prah
description: Longest natural cave in South Asia and India, stretching over 30-34 km in the Shnongrim Ridge, with vast chambers including the Aircraft Hangar trunk passage, underground streams, and complex limestone formations. Adventure caving destination.
facts: Longest cave in India/South Asia (~31-34 km mapped)
Near Shnongrim Ridge, East Jaintia Hills
Best visited dry season Nov-May; guided exploration

name: Narpuh Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Wildlife sanctuary covering about 60 sq km of semi-evergreen and evergreen forests in the southern East Jaintia Hills, protecting threatened species including hoolock gibbons, hornbills and other Northeast fauna. Notified in 2014.
facts: Southern East Jaintia Hills near Lumshnong
Important for western hoolock gibbon and hornbills
Only major protected area in Jaintia Hills region

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Iconic turquoise-blue waterfall in Amlarem subdivision cascading into a natural pool amid dense forests. Popular for swimming (life jackets available), photography and short treks; one of Meghalaya’s most photogenic falls.
facts: About 30 km from Jowai and 90 km from Shillong

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic stones in Meghalaya at Nartiang village, former summer capital of the Jaintia kings. Features tall menhirs (up to 8 m) and dolmens erected 16th–19th centuries to honour ancestors and warriors.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient Shakti Peeth temple dedicated to Goddess Durga (worshipped as Jayanti) in Nartiang. One of 51 Shakti Peethas; site of major Durga Puja celebrations and historic Jaintia royal association.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and crystal-clear Umngot River famous for transparent waters where boats appear to float in air during winter. Features historic 1932 suspension bridge and India-Bangladesh border views.
facts: Famous for crystal-clear riverbed visibility in winter

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village on the Umngot River upstream from Dawki, hub for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, snorkeling and adventure tourism in a quieter setting with white sandy beaches.
facts: Popular for riverside camping and water sports
Cleaner and less crowded stretch of Umngot

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake near Jowai, created according to legend by the followers of chieftain Sajar Nangli. Scenic picnic spot with boating, surrounded by pine forests and hills.
facts: About 8–10 km from Jowai on NH6
Legend linked to Sajar Nangli exodus
Popular local picnic and leisure spot
Also known as Pung Sajar Nangli

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong–Jowai road, cascading over rocky cliffs into a pool amid paddy fields. Accessible via short walk from an arch bridge viewpoint.
facts: Short walk via picturesque arch bridge

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters town of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Gateway to district attractions with markets, churches and views of the Myntdu River valley.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills since 2012
Main base for exploring the district

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Offbeat two-tiered waterfall near Jarain/Shkentalang with emerald plunge pools, reached by a moderate trek through forest and rocky paths. Associated with Paradise Adventure Camp.

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Historic riverside spot on the Myntdu River near Jowai meaning ‘golden flower’. Site of freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah’s resistance and a popular picnic area with suspension bridge and fish sanctuary.
facts: Site of U Kiang Nangbah freedom struggle

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai featuring sacred groves, walking trails and panoramic views of the Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Popular for picnics and nature walks.

name: Thlu Muwi Stone Bridge
description: Historic megalithic stone bridge built by Jaintia warriors for the king’s passage over the Muwi stream during monsoons. Adjacent to Muwi Waterfalls; located on the Jowai–Dawki road.
facts: Built for Jaintia king’s monsoon passage

name: Umiam Lake (Barapani)
description: Scenic man-made reservoir created by damming the Umiam River in the early 1960s, about 15-17 km north of Shillong. Known as Barapani (Big Water), it offers water sports, boating, viewpoints, and is flanked by pine-clad hills. Major gateway attraction on the Guwahati-Shillong route.
facts: Created by damming Umiam River in early 1960s
About 15-17 km from Shillong on NH6
Popular for kayaking, boating and water sports
First major hydroelectric reservoir in Northeast India

name: Lum Nehru Park
description: Charming landscaped park adjacent to Umiam Lake and Orchid Lake Resort, featuring lawns, flower beds, orchidarium and aviary. Ideal for picnics and quiet walks overlooking the lake.
facts: Adjacent to Umiam Lake and Orchid Lake Resort

name: Lum Sohpetbneng (Navel of Heaven)
description: Sacred Khasi peak known as the Navel of Heaven, central to Khasi mythology as the site of a golden ladder connecting heaven and earth. Offers panoramic views of Umiam Lake and surrounding hills; site of annual Seng Khasi pilgrimage.
facts: Sacred site in Khasi cosmology (Hynniewtrep origin)
About 25-26 km from Shillong near Umiam
Annual pilgrimage on first Sunday of February

name: Dwar Ksuid (Devil’s Doorway)
description: Unique natural rock formation resembling a doorway on a river in the Bhoilymbong/Umroi area, known as Devil’s Doorway or Lover’s Paradise. Features swift-flowing river, slippery boulders and scenic picnic spots.
facts: Located in Khapmara, Bhoilymbong area near Umroi
About 17 km from Shillong / near airport

name: Nongkhyllem Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of about 29 sq km in Ri-Bhoi district covering subtropical forests, home to elephants, leopards, hoolock gibbons, capped langurs, hornbills and rich birdlife. Established in 1981 from earlier reserved forest.
facts: Important for western hoolock gibbon and hornbills

name: Nongpoh
description: Headquarters town of Ri-Bhoi district on NH6, midway between Guwahati and Shillong. Gateway to Umiam Lake, Nongkhyllem Sanctuary, Umden silk villages and northern Meghalaya.
facts: About 52 km from Shillong and 48 km from Guwahati

name: Umden-Diwon Eri Silk Village
description: Cluster of villages in Ri-Bhoi known as Meghalaya’s first official Eri Silk Village, producing ethical Ahimsa/Peace Silk (Ryndia) using traditional handlooms. GI-tagged craft, women-led cooperatives, surrounded by sacred groves and pineapples.
facts: Declared first Eri Silk Village of Meghalaya in 2021
About 70 km from Shillong, 28 km from Nongpoh
Women-led handloom cooperatives and GI tag

name: Marngar Lake
description: Serene natural lake near Marngar village in Ri-Bhoi, offering quiet scenic views and local picnic opportunities amid the district’s green hills.
